problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$

activity_context.topic_title: Shear and Stretch as Linear Transformations

feedback.problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis. Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we are told that $T$ represents a stretch along the $x$-axis or $y$-axis.

Comparing the $x$- and $y$-components of $v$ and $T(v),$ we note the following:

- the $x$-components of $v$ and $T(v)$ are the same, while

- the $y$-component of $T(v)$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ times the $y$-component of $v.$

So, we conclude that $T$ represents a stretch of scale factor $\frac{1}{3}$ in the $y$-direction.

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
